title: S2 auto-answer: how to treat the rule seam (resolveByCompiledRule)
context: Issue #517 scope point 1 lists the auto-answer chain as findReusableDecision -> resolveByCompiledRule -> findDecisionPrecedents. But resolveByCompiledRule (decision-resolver.ts:60) matches COMPILED RULES by trigger_patterns against a packet's touched FILES, then picks the option carrying per-option file/rule evidence. A PipelineQuestion is plain-language (business_text + outcome-string options + one grounded_in ref); it has no touched files and no per-option rule evidence, so the rule seam can only either no-op always (dead code, hurts the 95% branch gate) or pick options[0] arbitrarily (a wrong 'answer'). The two other seams fit a free-text question naturally: findReusableDecision (exact/fingerprint reuse via a synthesized intake.requirement packet) and findDecisionPrecedents (deterministic textual jaccard, high-confidence only). All three are zero-token lookups.

options.label: Wire the two applicable seams only (findReusableDecision -> findDecisionPrecedents); document the rule seam as inapplicable to plain-language questions. Cleanest and honest, no dead code.
Wire all three verbatim; thread grounded_in into the synthetic packet so resolveByCompiledRule CAN fire when a question carries file/rule evidence (rare), covered by a contrived test.
Replace the rule seam with the exported resolveDecisionPacket full chain (rule->design-system->profile->rag), accepting only source==='rule' so semantic-rag never auto-answers.

rationale: Rule seam is file-glob-triggered and cannot meaningfully choose among plain-language outcome options; wiring it is dead code or arbitrary picks. Chain the two seams that fit a free-text question: findReusableDecision (exact reuse) then findDecisionPrecedents (textual, high-confidence).
